sources.title: Instances of Computational Optimal Recovery: Dealing with Observation Errors
sources.read_scope: Introduction through §2.1 Theorem 1 and its dual-LP proof (PDF pp.1–5 / returned lines0–209).
sources.finding: The target may be a vector of linear functionals with sup-norm error. The local consistency set and ambient-output LP are established. Setting observation error to zero covers the old exact-summary model. The theorem does not impose output membership in that source or evaluate the report’s reset-family compatible-radius equality.
sources.impact: Credit generic recovery and the finite solver; retain only the proved family-specific construction as the local delta.

sources.title: A numerical algorithm for attaining the Chebyshev bound in optimal learning
sources.read_scope: Introduction relative-center definition equation(2), contribution statement and §2 opening definition of the consistent model class (returned lines60–118).
sources.finding: The output-constrained min–max objective is a relative-center problem. Selecting the feasible query image as the output set expresses compatible recovery. This is a formulation comparison, not an application of the source’s numerical algorithm or complexity claims.
sources.impact: Compatibility itself is established methodology; equality of restricted and ambient optima still needs the specialized proof.

sources.title: Chain algebras of finite distributive lattices
sources.read_scope: Theorem3.4 and complete three-step maximal-chain-vector proof (returned lines216–241); preceding ideal-lattice definition lines110–121.
sources.finding: The maximal-chain-vector span has dimension |L|−|P| for L=J(P). The equal-price connection is a direct antecedent, rather than a novel generic rank principle.
sources.impact: Keep the report’s explicit credit and restrict the claimed calculation to weighted intersection, actual-mean repair and compatible recovery.
